subtitle: When scripture, empire and silence met the widow’s flame

panels.shot: split-frame wide, half in Calcutta ghat, half in London council chamber
panels.action: On one side, Rammohun Roy stands on a smoky riverside beside a looming funeral pyre; on the other, Lord William Bentinck leans over a desk piled with reports, both faces lit by the same imagined flame.

dialogue.text: Between the widow’s pyre and the Governor-General’s desk, Rammohun Roy and Lord William Bentinck faced a burning question: who speaks when a tradition takes a woman’s life?

i18n.hi: विधवा की चिता से लेकर गवर्नर जनरल की मेज तक, राममोहन राय और लॉर्ड विलियम बेंटिंक एक सवाल से जले: जब रिवाज किसी स्त्री की जान ले, तो बोलता कौन है?

panels.shot: somber wide of riverside cremation ground at dawn
panels.action: A Bengal cremation ghat stretches along the river in misty light; in the distance, faint figures gather around a tall stacked pyre, the river surface dull and heavy.

dialogue.text: In the 1810s, colonial records in Bengal counted hundreds of widow burnings each year; in 1818 alone, officials noted 839 cases on ghats like this.

i18n.hi: १८१० के दशक में, बंगाल के हुकूमती कागज़ों में हर साल सैकड़ों सती दर्ज हुईं; सिर्फ १८१८ में ही ऐसे घाटों पर ८३९ मामले लिखे गए।

panels.shot: close-up on Rammohun Roy watching a distant pyre, side profile
panels.action: Rammohun Roy stands apart from the crowd, gaze fixed on the distant pyre, his jaw clenched, his scholar’s shawl wrapped tightly against the river breeze.

dialogue.text: A young Bengali intellectual, Rammohun Roy, watched such fires with unease, asking not only what happened there, but why scripture and society allowed it.

i18n.hi: एक युवा बंगाली बुद्धिजीवी, राममोहन राय, इन अग्नियों को घबराहट से देखता रहा, पूछता रहा कि यहाँ क्या होता है — और क्यों धरम और समाज इसे मान लेते हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot interior of a modest Calcutta study, lamplight, papers scattered
panels.action: Inside a Calcutta room lit by an oil lamp, Rammohun Roy sits cross-legged amid open Sanskrit texts, Persian manuscripts and English books, pen poised over a draft.

dialogue.text: Roy turned to texts and print, arguing from Vedic and Shastric verses that burning widows alive had no binding scriptural command, and could be opposed as a human duty.

i18n.hi: राय ने ग्रंथों और छपाई का सहारा लिया, वेदिक और शास्त्रीय श्लोकों से दिखाया कि विधवाओं को जिंदा जलाने का कोई पक्का हुक्म नहीं, और इंसानी फर्ज़ से इसका विरोध होना चाहिए।

panels.shot: low-angle close on a pamphlet in Roy’s hand
panels.action: Rammohun’s hand holds a freshly printed pamphlet, its pages dense; behind him, a small Bengali press clatters as workers stack more sheets.

dialogue.text: In his Conference between an Advocate for and an Opponent of the Practice of Burning Widows Alive, Roy staged a fierce debate on paper, line by line.

i18n.hi: अपनी किताब ‘विधवाओं को जीवित जलाने के पक्ष और विपक्ष में बातचीत’ में, राय ने कागज़ पर तीखी बहस खड़ी की, पंक्ति दर पंक्ति।

dialogue.speaker: rammohun_roy_and_lord_william_bentinck
dialogue.text: Where is the divine order that commands a woman to die with her husband?

i18n.hi: कहाँ है वो ईश्वरी आदेश जो स्त्री को पति संग मरने को कहे?

panels.shot: medium shot of a public reading in a Calcutta courtyard
panels.action: Rammohun stands in a courtyard reading aloud from his work to a mixed group of Bengali men in traditional dress and some in European clothes; some nod, others frown.

dialogue.text: He used meetings, petitions and newspapers to spread his argument: that compassion and interpretation, not unchallenged custom, should guide Hindu practice.

i18n.hi: उसने सभा, दरख़्वास्तें और अखबारों का सहारा लिया, फैलाते हुए अपनी बात: कि हिंदू आचार को अंधी रिवायत नहीं, करुणा और समझ से चलना चाहिए।

panels.shot: medium shot of a conservative gathering, contrasting mood
panels.action: In another Calcutta hall, Radhakanta Deb stands amid conservative elites; a large scroll lies open on a low table as men debate earnestly.

dialogue.text: But many powerful Hindus rejected interference. Radhakanta Deb and others formed the Dharma Sabha, readying petitions to defend what they saw as sacred tradition.

i18n.hi: पर कई ताकतवर हिंदुओं ने दख़ल मानने से इंकार किया। राधाकांत देब और साथियों ने धर्मसभा बनाई, दरख़्वास्तें तैयार कीं ताकि जिस रिवाज को पवित्र मानते थे, उसे बचा सकें।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye of Calcutta streets with signs of British rule
panels.action: A wide view of Calcutta shows the Hooghly river, Company buildings with flagpoles, Indian neighbourhoods, and a carriage carrying British officials along the road.

dialogue.text: Over all this hung Company power. British officials claimed neutrality in religion, yet they collected data on sati and debated how far law could reach into custom.

i18n.hi: सबके ऊपर कंपनी की ताकत तनी थी। अंग्रेज अफ़सर खुद को धर्म में तटस्थ कहते, पर सती के आँकड़े जुटाते और सोचते कि क़ानून रिवाज में कितनी दूर घुस सकता है।

panels.shot: interior wide of Government House in Calcutta, council table
panels.action: Lord William Bentinck sits at the head of a long table in Government House, reports and tables before him; other councillors listen as he points to a document.

dialogue.text: When William Bentinck became Governor-General, he received detailed returns on sati and reformist petitions on one side, conservative counter-petitions on the other.

i18n.hi: जब विलियम बेंटिंक गवर्नर जनरल बना, उसे एक तरफ़ सती के चिट्ठे और सुधारवादी दरख़्वास्तें मिलीं, दूसरी तरफ़ रिवाज बचाने वाली सख़्त अरज़ियाँ।

panels.shot: close-up on Bentinck’s face, lit by lamplight, thoughtful
panels.action: Bentinck leans over a report, his brow furrowed, lamplight reflecting off his spectacles as the murmur of the council fades behind him.

dialogue.text: His minutes reveal tension: respect for property and ‘native usage’ weighed against the stark fact that the usage meant a widow’s death, again and again.

i18n.hi: उसकी टिप्पणियाँ एक खिंचाव दिखाती हैं: ज़मीन और ‘मूल रिवाज’ का सम्मान, बनाम ये साफ़ सच कि वही रिवाज बार‑बार विधवा की मौत मांगता है।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a council chamber as a decision is announced
panels.action: The council chamber is still; Bentinck sits upright as clerks wait with quills. Outside the windows, a grey sky hangs over Calcutta.

dialogue.text: In late 1829, after debate and consultation, Bentinck chose a path: to treat sati not as protected ritual, but as a crime under Company law.

i18n.hi: १८२९ के आखिर में, बहस और सलाह के बाद बेंटिंक ने रास्ता चुना: सती को बची हुई पूजा नहीं, कंपनी के क़ानून के तहत जुर्म मानना।

dialogue.speaker: rammohun_roy_and_lord_william_bentinck
dialogue.text: We cannot remain passive while life is taken before our eyes.

i18n.hi: हम आँखों के सामने जान जाती देख, चुप नहीं खड़े रह सकते।

panels.shot: close-up on an official parchment being signed
panels.action: A hand in European dress holds a quill over an official parchment; the scripted heading of Bengal Regulation XVII lies open as the pen touches the page.

dialogue.text: On 4 December 1829, Bengal Regulation XVII was signed, abolishing sati in British Bengal and declaring assistance or participation punishable.

i18n.hi: ४ दिसंबर १८२९ को बंगाल विनियम सत्रह पर दस्तख़त हुए, ब्रिटिश बंगाल में सती ख़त्म कर दी गई, और मदद या शिरकत को सज़ायोग्य ठहराया गया।

panels.shot: medium shot at a village ghat with officials present
panels.action: At a rural ghat, a would-be funeral pyre stands unfinished; a British Indian officer and local policemen speak with male relatives, the widow seated aside, veiled and silent.

dialogue.text: In practice, the new law meant officials could intervene, halt preparations, and prosecute those arranging a sati—but it did not rewrite widowhood itself.

i18n.hi: असल में नए क़ानून ने अफ़सरों को हस्तक्षेप का हक़ दिया—तैयारियाँ रोकने और सती करवाने वालों पर मुक़दमा चलाने का—लेकिन विधवा‑जीवन खुद नहीं बदला।

panels.shot: interior wide of a Calcutta conservative meeting drafting a petition
panels.action: Radhakanta Deb and Dharma Sabha members sit around low desks, drafting a long petition; their faces are tense, some gesturing toward the direction of Government House.

dialogue.text: Dharma Sabha leaders answered with a massive petition to the Company and to Britain, insisting that the ban violated religious freedom and ancient dharma.

i18n.hi: धर्मसभा के नेताओं ने कंपनी और ब्रिटेन को एक भारी भरकम दरख़्वास्त भेजी, कहकर कि ये पाबंदी धार्मिक आज़ादी और सनातन धर्म पर चोट है।

panels.shot: split composition of London and Calcutta documents being handled
panels.action: On one side, clerks in Calcutta dispatch bound copies of Regulation XVII and petitions; on the other, London officials in frock coats receive them in a paneled office.

dialogue.text: The argument crossed oceans. In London, reformers and Company directors examined the ban, weighing rights of worship against the question of widow sacrifice.

i18n.hi: बहस समंदर पार चली गई। लंदन में सुधारक और कंपनी हाकिम इस रोक को परखते रहे, पूजा के हक़ को विधवा बलि के सवाल के साथ तौलते रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Roy in London, looking out at streets
panels.action: Rammohun Roy, now in European dress with an Indian turban, stands at a London window, looking out at a grey street, folded papers in his hand.

dialogue.text: Roy himself traveled to Britain, praised by some as a reformer, but he was one voice among many in the wider imperial debates on India, religion and law.

i18n.hi: राय खुद इंग्लैंड गया, कुछ के लिए सुधारक, मगर भारत, धर्म और क़ानून पर बड़े साम्राज्यवादी झगड़ों में वह भी कई आवाज़ों में बस एक आवाज़ था।

panels.shot: close-up on a single veiled widow’s face, eyes lowered
panels.action: A Bengali widow sits indoors on a mat, head shaved, simple white sari pulled over her head; her face is partly in shadow, eyes downcast.

dialogue.text: Feminist historians later asked: through all this paper—pamphlets, petitions, regulations—where were the widows’ own voices, their words about the lives they lived?

i18n.hi: नारीवादी इतिहासकारों ने बाद में पूछा: इन ढेरों कागज़ों—पुस्तिकाओं, दरख़्वास्तों, नियमों—की भीड़ में विधवाओं की अपनी आवाज़ कहाँ थी, उनकी ज़िंदगी की ज़ुबान कहाँ थी?

panels.shot: wide of village life with a widow working, boys playing nearby
panels.action: In a Bengal village, a widow quietly carries water while children play; elders sit discussing news, oblivious to her labor and isolation.

dialogue.text: The law stopped legal burnings in Company territory, but poverty, shaved heads, food taboos and stigma endured; elsewhere in India, forms of sati persisted beyond 1829.

i18n.hi: क़ानून ने कंपनी के इलाक़े में सती को क़ानूनी तौर पर रोका, पर गरीबी, मुड़वा सिर, खाने की पाबंदियाँ और कलंक बने रहे; भारत के और हिस्सों में, सती की शक्लें १८२९ के बाद भी टिकी रहीं।

panels.shot: final wide frame blending pyre smoke into stacks of records
panels.action: Smoke from a now-unlit pyre rises and fades into shelves of court records and pamphlets; faint silhouettes of Rammohun Roy and Bentinck stand apart, turned toward the unseen figure of a widow.

dialogue.text: Rammohun Roy and Bentinck helped turn fire into felony, yet the story reminds us: a humane law is only the beginning, unless those it claims to protect can finally speak for themselves.

i18n.hi: राममोहन राय और बेंटिंक ने आग को अपराध बनाया, फिर भी कहानी याद दिलाती है: इंसाफ़ी क़ानून बस शुरुआत है, जब तक जिन्हें बचाने का दावा है, वे खुद खुलकर बोल सकें।

subtitle_i18n.en: When scripture, empire and silence met the widow’s flame
subtitle_i18n.hi: जब धर्मग्रंथ, साम्राज्य और सन्नाटा विधवा की लौ से टकराए
